Definition: from G575 and G4126; to set sail:--sail away.
BiblicalUsage: To set sail — four times, and every sailing is a leg of Paul's journeys. Being sent forth by the Holy Ghost, they sailed to Cyprus in Acts 13:4, and sailed back to Antioch in Acts 14:26, from whence they had been recommended to the grace of God. The voyage to Miletus runs day by day in Acts 20:15, and the last sailing begins in Acts 27:1, when it was determined that they should sail into Italy.
TheologicalSignificance: I love how Luke logs the sailings the way a sailor would: sent forth, recommended, arrived, determined. The gospel travelled by ship, and every departure was either the Spirit's sending or God's determination. My own goings are no less ordered — the winds and the timetables both belong to Him.
